summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. Despite normal lipase and white blood cell count, her symptoms and history supported a diagnosis of acute on chronic pancreatitis, possibly due to pancreatic burnout. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, IV pain and nausea control, and temporary discontinuation of TPN. Her diet was advanced to sips and then clear liquids by hospital day three, and she transitioned to oral pain and nausea medications. TPN was restarted. Her pancytopenia persisted despite holding potential myelosuppressive agents (Compazine, Phenergan), prompting a recommendation for hematologic follow-up. She remained stable, with no complications, and was discharged home with continued TPN, her baseline medications, and follow-up plans with GI and hematology.
